blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
Robot learning in simulation depends on the objects the simulator offers.
Many tasks need objects with separate parts, joints that allow the required
motion, and physical properties that remain valid under contact. Existing methods recover this structure anew for every image: generative models predict parts and joints that mostly fail to settle or move in simulation, and general-purpose agents need a long session of model calls for each photograph. AffordCraft builds
such an asset from a single RGB image and a task instruction by retrieval
instead of generation: it locates the object and the part to operate,
selects a matching entry from a library of articulated assets, and fits it
to the image while keeping its parts and joints intact. Without any box or
mask marking the object, AffordCraft produces a physically valid asset for
1,703 of 2,000 photographs from 31 categories. Five generative methods pass
on at most 45% of the same photographs and, at the median, need 10 to 78
times our GPU time per valid asset. On 50 cluttered images, 162 of 237
annotated objects pass the same physical test after automatic detection.
Growing the library from 141 to 11,372 entries needs no change to the method
and raises category coverage from 46% to 100% and the share of selections
with the requested label from 18% to 51%. We also build manipulation
tasks from the constructed assets, both with single objects and in composed
scenes; policies trained on scripted demonstrations complete both kinds of
tasks from initial states unseen in training.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Simulation eliminates the hardware, operator time, and repeated resets required by experiments with real objects ( Chen et al., 2026b ; Ranawaka et al., 2026 ) . Its usefulness, however, is fundamentally limited by the quality of the assets it contains. Many everyday objects are articulated: cabinet doors rotate about hinges, drawers translate along rails, and storage bins slide within frames. To reproduce their behavior, a simulator must represent them as multiple rigid bodies connected by joints, equipped with appropriate collision geometry and physical parameters that remain stable under contact. Constructing such assets manually is labor-intensive and difficult to scale.
blocks.zh: 模拟消除了实际物体实验所需的硬件,操作时间和重复重置(Chen等,2026b;Ranawaka等,2026.). 但是,它的效用从根本上受到它所含资产质量的限制。 许多日常物品被拼接:柜门围绕链条旋转,抽屉会沿着铁道翻译,而存储箱在框内滑行. 为了复制他们的行为,一个模拟器必须代表他们作为由关节相接的多根刚性体,并配备适当的相撞几何和在接触下保持稳定的物理参数. 人工建造这种资产是劳动密集型的,难以扩大规模。

blocks.en: A mesh may visually resemble a cabinet while lacking any explicit representation of its door, hinge, or interior structure. Existing automatic methods typically recover this information independently for each input image, making the process both expensive and difficult to generalize. Generative models can infer geometry and articulation from photographs ( Cao et al., 2026b ; Cao et al., 2026a ; Liu et al., 2026 ) , but their predictions often fail to produce physically valid assets: parts may not rest stably, contacts may be inconsistent, and articulated components may not move as intended (Table 1 ). General-purpose agents can construct functional assets through modeling tools ( Guo, 2026 ; Ding et al., 2026 ) , yet doing so for a single photograph may require a lengthy sequence of model calls and substantial tool interaction.

blocks.en: Crucially, the articulation structures of everyday objects are highly repetitive. A drawer, for example, may slide along the same axis in both a desk and a filing cabinet. This observation suggests replacing open-ended reconstruction with retrieval and adaptation from a library of articulated, part-decomposed assets. Such libraries mitigate the cost of modeling and physical validation: each mechanism is constructed and verified once, then reused across many objects. Given an image, selecting and fitting a suitable library asset transforms single-view reconstruction from an unconstrained generation problem into a constrained matching problem over known mechanisms. The resulting system can therefore produce physically grounded simulation assets more efficiently, reliably, and consistently.
blocks.zh: 关键的是,日常物体的表达结构非常重复. 例如,抽屉可以沿着同一个轴线在桌子和档案柜上滑行。 这一意见建议用从一个由部分分解的明细资产组成的图书馆取回和改造来取代开放式重建。 此类库可以减轻模型和物理验证的成本:每个机制都构造和核实一次,然后在许多物体上重复使用。 考虑到图像,选择和安装合适的图书馆资产,将单一视图重建从不受限制的生成问题转变为超出已知机制的限制匹配问题。 因此,由此产生的系统可以更有效地、可靠地和一致地产生实际存在的模拟资产。

blocks.en:
We present AffordCraft, which builds a task-ready simulation asset from one RGB
image and a task instruction (Figures 1 and 2 ). It locates the object and the part the task acts on
and determines the required motion, such as a rotation about a hinge. It then
retrieves library entries by category and visual similarity, and a multimodal
model checks which of them provide that motion at the right part, or abstains
if none does. Finally, it scales and places the chosen entry without changing
its parts or joints, and accepts the result only if it passes a physical test
in simulation. The image encoder and the multimodal model can be exchanged,
and the library grows by adding entries.

A cabinet of another color is usable as long as its door hinges where the task
requires. Assets that share a mechanism but differ in appearance also give
policy training the appearance variation of several objects, which a single
exact copy does not.

blocks.en:
Our contributions are: • Structure built once and reused. Parts, joints, and physical
parameters are modeled and checked once, in the library; construction selects
among them instead of estimating them for every image. AffordCraft delivers a physically valid asset for 85% of 2,000 photographs, at a median
of 40 s per input on one RTX 5090 and 0.8 GPU-minutes per valid asset, while
generative methods reach at most 45% and need 8–63 GPU-minutes under the
same protocol and test (Table 1 ). Growing the library from 141 to
11,372 entries improves coverage and selection, and retrieval stays near
50 ms. • Task-conditioned construction under a physical gate. The
instruction fixes which part must move and how. A multimodal selector checks
each candidate against its recorded structure and rejects 1,093 of the 5,874
candidate attempts, adaptation keeps the selected bodies and joints, and an
asset is accepted only after it passes a physical test in simulation. Removing
the task condition costs 22 percentage points of correctly built assets,
removing the articulation adapter 40, and removing physical-feedback
reselection 11 (Table 2 ). • Large-scale evaluation. We evaluate on
2,000 photographs from 31 categories and on 50 cluttered images with 237
annotated objects, always from the full image with no box or mask. Seven
external methods are scored by the same test as ours, five of them on all
2,000 inputs: an asset counts only if it exports, carries valid inertia,
settles under gravity, rests on real support, and moves at the requested
part.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
PartNet and SAPIEN provide part-annotated, articulated objects for interactive
simulation ( Mo et al., 2019 ; Xiang et al., 2020 ) . Large object and scene
collections add appearance and layout at
scale ( Deitke et al., 2023b ; Deitke et al., 2023a ; Wu et al., 2023 ; Fu et al., 2021 ; Dai et al., 2017 ) ,
but they lack the moving parts and joints that manipulation needs. Because
articulated assets are built by hand, another line of work recovers geometry
from images, with multi-view neural fields and surface
reconstruction ( Mildenhall et al., 2020 ; Müller et al., 2022 ; Kerbl et al., 2023 ; Wang et al., 2021 ; Yariv et al., 2021 ; Barron et al., 2022 ; Li et al., 2023 ) or with feed-forward and generative models that use one or a few
views ( Yu et al., 2021 ; Hong et al., 2024 ; Liu et al., 2023b ; Long et al., 2024 ; Xu et al., 2024 ; Jun & Nichol, 2023 ; Nichol et al., 2022 ) .
These methods return a surface, not a mechanism. Part-level methods track
articulated poses and locate actionable
parts ( Weng et al., 2021 ; Mo et al., 2021 ; Geng et al., 2023 ) ;
Articulate-Anything infers articulation with a vision-language
model ( Le et al., 2025 ) ; and PhysX-Anything, PhysX-Omni, and PAct
generate geometry together with parts or physical
attributes ( Cao et al., 2026a ; Cao et al., 2026b ; Liu et al., 2026 ) . None of
these routes produces, from one photograph and at scale, an asset whose parts
and joints a simulator can operate: generators return a surface or an
unverified guess of the joints, and part-level methods assume that the object
already exists as a mesh or a dataset entry. Section 4.2 measures this gap with one physical test. AffordCraft instead starts from the
requested interaction and selects a mechanism that the library already holds.

blocks.en:
Embodied platforms and manipulation benchmarks come with fixed object
sets ( Brockman et al., 2016 ; Kolve et al., 2017 ; Savva et al., 2019 ; Szot et al., 2021 ; James et al., 2020 ; Yu et al., 2019 ; Mees et al., 2022 ; Mu et al., 2021 ; Gu et al., 2023 ; Nasiriany et al., 2024 ; Makoviychuk et al., 2021 ) ,
and SimFoundry assembles interchangeable components into scenes that preserve
affordances ( Ranawaka et al., 2026 ) . General multimodal agents can
already build interactive assets: GPT-6 Astra projects replay robot episodes
in simulation ( Guo, 2026 ; Ding et al., 2026 ) . Such an
agent rediscovers the mechanism in a session of many model calls for every
photograph.
On our 200-input subset it produces a physically valid asset for 34.5% of the
inputs, at a median of 24 minutes and 2.90 USD of model calls per input
(Table 1 , Appendix A.9 ). In AffordCraft the structure is recorded once in the
library and reused by every query.

blocks.en:
Much recent work on policy learning builds on interactive environments.
RoboTwin 2.0 generates demonstrations at scale, RoboDojo benchmarks generalist
policies, and MimicGen multiplies a few human demonstrations into
many ( Chen et al., 2026b ; Chen et al., 2026a ; Mandlekar et al., 2023 ) .
Policies from RT-1 and PaLM-E to OpenVLA, Octo, and Diffusion Policy learn
from such interactions and from open robot
datasets ( Brohan et al., 2023 ; Driess et al., 2023 ; Ahn et al., 2022 ; Open X-Embodiment Collaboration, 2024 ; Zhao et al., 2023 ; Kim et al., 2024 ; Kim et al., 2025 ; Octo Model Team et al., 2024 ; Chi et al., 2023 ) ,
and their transfer to hardware relies on randomized and offline
data ( Peng et al., 2018 ; Mandlekar et al., 2021 ) . All of them
depend on the available object set: a task can be demonstrated or scored only
if some object provides the required motion. AffordCraft supplies such objects as
the bodies, joints, and physical parameters that simulators accept, and
leaves the policy architecture open; Section 4.5 trains
policies on constructed assets.

blocks.en:
The task query, the ranking features, the body–joint structure, and the
physical gate are separate modules, so the library grows without changes to
perception or selection. New instances of a category add substitutes for
tasks that are already covered; new categories and mechanisms add tasks that
no earlier entry supports. We report category coverage, the fraction of
queries whose requested category the library contains. More entries cannot
lower coverage, but they enlarge the pool and can change the selector’s choice, and a correctly selected entry
can still fail to settle, so we measure coverage, selection quality, and
physical pass rate separately.

blocks.en: 5 Discussion and Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5. 讨论和结论

blocks.en:
AffordCraft builds simulation-ready assets from RGB images and task
instructions by retrieving and adapting library assets rather than
reconstructing them for each image. It selects assets with the required
parts and joints, preserves their mechanisms during adaptation, and
validates the outputs in simulation. The method produces assets that
pass the physical gate for 1,703 of 2,000 photographs and 162 of 237
annotated objects in cluttered images. The same pipeline supports
library growth from 141 to 11,372 entries. Across the five
libraries, coverage rises only when new categories arrive (46% to 100%),
while top-1 agreement rises at every step (18% to 51%). In the ten
scenes the scripted teacher completes 273 of 320 episodes, and heads trained
on scripted demonstrations complete tasks of both kinds from unseen initial
states.

Limitations. Our single-object evaluation measures asset construction when the object
category is given in the instruction, rather than open-vocabulary
recognition. Category coverage and top-1 agreement compare labels, not
whether the selected asset has the right part and motion for the task.
We evaluate objects in cluttered images individually, without assessing
scene depth, support relations, or layout. Small differences in the
ablations are not enough to establish a reliable improvement. The
manipulation tasks use a fixed set of assets seen during development, so
generalization to unseen assets and transfer to real robots remain to be
tested, and independent part annotations with scene-level evaluation
would let us assess task matching and spatial structure more directly.

One part of the pipeline is not deterministic. The convex decomposition takes
frozen parameters at each level of the cascade but no random seed, so building
the collision geometry of a mesh again can return a different set of hulls,
and with it a different verdict for a borderline asset. The campaign avoids
this within itself by caching the decomposition under a key built from the
source mesh and the cascade version: every worker that met a mesh again read
the stored hulls, so one realization is fixed across the whole run and across
the ablations that reuse the cache. Reproducing the numbers from an empty
cache reruns the decomposition and need not land on that same realization.

blocks.en:
The columns of Table 1 are defined as follows. Export is the
share of inputs that end with a structured asset. Native scores that asset as
delivered at the physical gate of Section 3.3 , adapted scores
it after our common physical adaptation, and articulated is the share of
inputs whose accepted asset carries at least one movable joint. Median time is
the median end-to-end (E2E) wall-clock time from input to validated asset in
the clean timing run. GPU minutes per pass divides that time by the pass rate
of the row, giving the cost of an accepted asset at the median; a worker holds
one GPU, so its worker-minutes are GPU-minutes. Pass in 5 min is the share of
the timed inputs whose asset clears the gate within five minutes of wall time,
one point of the curves in Figure 5 , which scores each
external method on its native path where that applies and on the adapted one
otherwise, with the time of that build. Peak is the largest device memory in
use on the worker’s GPU. For every
local method these timing and resource cells come from the clean timing run (one
worker per exclusive RTX 5090, an RTX PRO 6000 for the PhysX-Omni geometry stage;
32 inputs of the registered subset) and the pass rates from the registered runs.
Table 9 lists the stage timing, wall-clock,
throughput, GPU, and monetary measurements of the matched full-RGB comparison
for every method. The E2E median
covers the complete construction and physical-validation path, not just
retrieval. Throughput counts physically accepted assets per hour; total cost
per valid asset includes failed attempts. API expense applies the model
providers’ official list prices to the token counts each run recorded:
gpt-6-astra at OpenAI’s Standard rates (10 USD per million input tokens,
1 for cached input, 12.50 for cache writes, 50 for output), gemini-2.5-flash
and gemini-3.8-flash at Google’s (0.30/2.50 and 0.75/3.75 USD). The relay
reports cached but not written prompt tokens, so every uncached agent prompt
token is billed as a cache write, an upper bound (2.56 USD per input at the
plain input rate). PartCrafter’s run keeps each part-count reply but not its
token count; its 0.005 USD per input uses the tokens the relay billed for
569 of its calls. The two API routes were not part of the clean timing
run (the relay had no credit then); their times are those of their own runs
over the 200 subset inputs.
AffordCraft is timed with the geometry of its library entries built once, the
regime in which every later query reuses it: a median of 40.0 s per input. Run
on the same 32 inputs from the geometry cache as it stood before the formal
campaign, it takes a median of 120.8 s, or 2.4 instead of 0.8 worker-minutes per
accepted asset at the median; the difference is geometry built once and reused
afterwards. Within five minutes of wall time, 53.1% of the timed inputs pass in this
regime and 43.8% from the pre-campaign cache, against at most 34.4% for any
other route (Figure 5 ). Twelve of the 32 inputs are
accepted within 30 s, before any other method has delivered one.
PhysX-Anything, the strongest generative method, accepts its first input in the
first minute and levels off at 20 of 32 after 15 minutes, where AffordCraft stands
at 21 and ends at 25. The two API routes accept 16% (Articulate-Anything) and
6% (the agent) of their 200 inputs within five minutes, and level off at 35%
and 34.5%. Means are higher (711 and 1,340 s) because a few inputs work through many
candidates and failed constructions are not cached (the slowest takes 8,825 s).

on the teacher episodes only, with correlated 0.005 rad noise added to the arm
joint inputs of 75% of the sequences. We then evaluate the checkpoint the run
registered at the end, fixed before any evaluation, and not a step picked once
the numbers were in.

The trained head and the untrained head (the same head with its random initial
weights) run the same 200 held-out initial states, and success is read from
simulator state and contacts, not from video. The trained head completes
114/200 episodes (57.0%, Wilson 95% interval 50.1–63.7%) against 1/200
for the untrained head, 58/100 on the rigid and 56/100 on the articulated
tasks, and it completes every task in at least 3 of its 20 episodes. Five
initial states of the articulated tasks produced no episode record in either
condition and count as failures; without them the rates are 114/195 and 1/195.
Of the trained head’s failures, 34 of 42 on the rigid tasks leave the object
outside the goal region or unstable, and 24 of 39 on the articulated tasks
command joint targets outside the admissible range. These ten assets were also in
use while the suite was developed. The study therefore shows that such tasks
can be learned from constructed assets; it says nothing about unseen ones.

The policy observes a fixed third-person camera (1280 × \times 960 render,
cropped to the workspace and resized to 320 × \times 240), a wrist camera on the
hand (70 ∘ field of view, 320 × \times 240), and its nine joint positions.
Both images pass with the instruction through the frozen OpenVLA-OFT
backbone ( Kim et al., 2025 ) , using its public LIBERO-Spatial
checkpoint ( Liu et al., 2023a ) . The mean of its 56 action-token states gives
a 4,096-d feature per image. The two features, concatenated, feed a recurrent
head (GRU, 512 units) that predicts eight future joint targets and executes
four at 10 Hz.
The backbone stays frozen, and the untrained condition is the same head with
its random initial weights.

Four collection workers recorded eight teacher episodes per scene each (320
episodes, 273 successes). A first head trained on 143 successful episodes drove
200 mixed rollouts in the manner of DAgger ( Ross et al., 2011 ) : the policy
executes bursts of 8–40 ticks inside the teacher’s plan, in half of the
rollouts also its first up to 200 ticks, at a target executed share of 0.35,
while the teacher supplies every label. A second head, trained on 267 teacher
successes and the 82 successful rollouts, drove 240 more. The final head trains
on the 267 teacher successes and 397 of the 440 rollouts, 214 of them
unsuccessful, 373,031 frames in total; the 216 rollouts that did not both pass
and complete the teacher’s plan are truncated 45 ticks before their end.
Excluded are teacher failures, rollouts shorter than 165 ticks or with an
object off the table, and 20 episodes whose executed eight-tick joint change
exceeds 0.75 rad. Training runs 24,000 AdamW steps (batch 16, learning rate 3 × 10 − 4 3\times 10^{-4} , cosine decay) on one A100 in 68 minutes, and again we
evaluate the checkpoint registered at the end.
